prompt_hardening.not-needed: Use when the execution/classification packet is already explicit and no missing acceptance, proof, material conflict or risky boundary needs added instruction framing.
prompt_hardening.micro: Use when a bounded task lacks one or more explicit acceptance, proof or observable details that can be added without a full authority and edge-case packet.
prompt_hardening.full: Use when cross-runtime governance explicitly requires Prompt A/B, or when material authority conflict, an incident without a reliable observable, irreversible production/security/authentication/secrets action, or architecture deadlock requires explicit authorities, boundaries, edge cases and stop conditions.

observable_status.not-applicable: Use only when no semantic or runtime decision needs an observable, such as deterministic mechanics.
observable_status.sufficient: Use when available authority, documentation, acceptance, proof and direct readback are sufficient to decide and verify the work.
observable_status.insufficient: Use when a required acceptance or proof condition, or a reliable runtime observable, is missing.
observable_status.conflicting: Use when material authorities or evidence conflict and direct readback cannot resolve them.

selection_rules.no-model: Prefer a deterministic script or shell command when no semantic judgment is required; do not launch another model merely for mechanics.
selection_rules.low: Use for bounded repository lookups, clear classifications, small patches and direct proof.
selection_rules.medium: Use for non-trivial engineering when repo-local AGENTS, observability, documentation and acceptance are sufficient.
selection_rules.high: Use only after an objective escalation trigger is proved and a complete receipt is recorded.

triggers.description: Repo-local authorities or evidence materially conflict and direct readback cannot resolve it.
An active incident or runtime decision lacks a reliable observable.
The decision is materially irreversible and affects production, security, authentication or secrets.
Materially different architectural choices remain and repo-local authority is insufficient.
Agent or forensic evidence conflicts and root readback cannot resolve it.

prohibitions.description: Do not escalate when an active coherent observable answers the decision.
Do not escalate when repo-local AGENTS, documentation and lifecycle rules answer the decision.
Do not escalate when scope, acceptance, proof and stop conditions are already bounded.
Do not escalate to reconcile claims that a direct root readback can resolve.
Project or issue priority HIGH is never a reasoning-effort trigger.
A bare request to use HIGH is insufficient without an objective trigger.
